action.new:
Reading the :attr:`port` attribute will raise a :exc:`ValueError` if
   an invalid port is specified in the URL.  See section
   :ref:`urlparse-result-object` for more information on the result object.

   Port validation is performed when the :attr:`port` attribute is
   accessed, not when the parsed result is constructed.  Both
   :func:`urlsplit` and :func:`urlparse` create their result object
   successfully regardless of the port value in the URL; a
   :exc:`ValueError` is raised only upon reading :attr:`port` if the
   port portion is not a non-negative ASCII integer in the range 0
   through 65535 (inclusive).

   .. doctest::
      :options: +NORMALIZE_WHITESPACE

      >>> from urllib.parse import urlsplit, urlparse
      >>> p = urlsplit("http://example.com:65536/")
      >>> p.port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
          ...
      ValueError: Port out of range 0-65535
      >>> p = urlsplit("http://example.com:0/")
      >>> p.port
      0
      >>> p = urlsplit("http://example.com:65535/")
      >>> p.port
      65535
      >>> p = urlsplit("http://example.com:abc/")
      >>> p.port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
          ...
      ValueError: Port could not be cast to integer value as 'abc'
      >>> p = urlparse("http://example.com:65536/")
      >>> p.port
      Traceback (most recent call last):
          ...
      ValueError: Port out of range 0-65535

   Unmatched square brackets in the :attr:`netloc` attribute will raise a
   :exc:`ValueError`.
